item.title: Majority of voters blame Taoiseach for Fianna Fáil presidential campaign
item.description: An overwhelming majority of voters are blaming the Taoiseach for Fianna Fail's botched presidential campaign. A new poll out today shows 68 percent believe Micheál Martin is responsible for the fiasco which has dogged the party internally since early October. The findings from the Sunday Independent/Ireland Thinks poll come ahead of the publication of an interval review into the selection of Jim Gavin as Fianna Fail's presidential candidate. item.title: All public car parks in Cavan Town now free ahead of Christmas
item.description: Car parking in Cavan Town is now free at all public car parks in the town. To support local business and encourage people to shop local this Christmas, Cavan County Council is making all off street parking (public carparks only) free in Cavan Town in the build up to the festive period. These include the car parks at the Courthouse, Townhall, Main Street, Bridge Street, Connolly Street and the Multistorey Carpark. item.title: No more road resurfacing funding expected for local authorities this year
item.description: A local TD has asked for clarification on whether Cavan and Monaghan County Councils will get additional funding for road resurfacing. item.title: Monaghan GP warns flu is hitting Ireland 'harder' this year
item.description: A Monaghan GP has warned that flu is hitting Ireland "harder" and even "earlier" this year. As we move into the Christmas season, Dr Ilona Duffy says more people will be gathered together and flu will rise rapidly as a result of that. While the local GP understands there is a certain element of vaccine fatigue, she warned that this year's flu outbreak has already led to fatalities. item.title: Glenullin break Cuchulain Ulster final hearts
item.description: Cuchulainn's fell to a five point defeat to Derry champions Glenullin in the Ulster intermediate championship. Goals in either half proved the difference for Glenullin as they won out 3-15 to 19 points. Cuchulainn's started stronger, racing into a four-point lead inside nine minutes with points from Adam O Reilly and Niall Magee.
